spec_notes: ratchet/spec.md is a list of use cases and clauses C-1..C-96; most of the unstated conditions in this share are marked "Open: The requester decides ..." (token precedence C-19, bot naming C-27, conversation labels C-28, draft/scroll C-31, overlapping sends C-33, interrupted replies C-39, library scope and name collisions C-45/C-50, edit-after-Use C-46, repeated/approximate memory facts C-56, eligible fields C-64, create id timing C-65, proposal lifetime C-66, conflicts C-69, Tasks scope C-76, absence C-81, steering target C-82, in-progress cancel C-84, auto-resume C-89, narrow layout C-92). The product then decides each of these (env token wins, unique names, per-person libraries with copy-at-Use, merge duplicate facts, id at confirm, one reply at a time, no auto-resume, conversation-scoped Tasks) but the specification still reads as open for them; the decisions live only in the README and code. Decided without being marked: C-57 pins a prefilled Memory text; C-14 pins server-side refusal for other persons' ids. Silent on: stored markers, management actions not adding messages, a second long task, task completion messages, field-name capitals, identifiers with a suffix (ORD-1001A), damaged data at start, write failures while running, focus after actions and server error logging. No clause contradicts the request.
tests_notes: npm test runs 14 tests. Two app tests bundle many behaviours: "setup, workspace libraries, bot memory, discussion context and guarded reply retry survive restart" covers setup refusal, new bot, instructions, memory edit, saved-task edit/run, retry idempotency and restart in one test, and "provider reviews and decisions are scoped, replay-safe and private" covers access, clarify, confirm, cross-person refusal, concurrent create and token secrecy. Several are tied to internals: "worker continues without polls..." reads DATA_DIR/state.json and its events array directly; the store test depends on the temporary file name state.next.json; tasks.test.js drives private task fields (claim, generation, attempts) and asserts attempts [1,2,1]; app tests assert the view's internal shape (turn.attempt, tasks[0].attempts[0]). Some would fail on another correct build: the app's own route names (retry-reply, retry-task, ack) and request bodies (operation, generation), ORD-1005/ORD-1006 allocation over all records, resume.activity[0].status. Nothing in npm test drives the page: Since-you-were-away rendering, focus, narrow layout, accessible names and Memory editing in the UI are untested by the suite (the acceptance/ harness is separate and not run by npm test).
maintainer: lib/app.js changeWorkspace is one long action switch where idempotency pre-checks run outside the store transaction and are repeated inside it, and replies and task steps commit through commitResult closures that retry on write failure; changing an action safely means keeping both copies of each guard and the attempt/generation counters in step. The front end (public/app.js) relies on 400 ms polling with epoch, selection and fetch-number checks to avoid painting stale or another person's data, which is easy to break when adding a new mutation. All state is one JSON snapshot cloned and rewritten on every change, so any schema change must also update the strict validate() in lib/store.js or the server refuses to start on existing data.
